paragraph: The telecoms regulator INACOM [relaunched its portal in June 2025 with a 24-hour AI chatbot](<https://inacom.gov.ao/2025/06/12/novo-portal-do-inacom-destaca-inovacao-ao-servico-do-cidadao/>). Expansão reported in November 2025 that the National Assembly [uses AI speech recognition to transcribe plenary sessions](<https://expansao.co.ao/angola/detalhe/banca-assembleia-nacional-sector-electrico-e-comercio-ja-dominam-uso-de-ia-68283.html>). That puts AI in service in two bodies. In the last twelve months, in January 2026, IGAPE said [its AI platform SEP360 was in its final phase](<https://targeting.ao/inteligencia-artificial/igape-considera-em-fase-final-plataforma-de-ia-para-o-sector-publico/>). No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of the government's AI systems, from the authority for cross-government digital governance.

In February 2025 the identification agency ANIP presented [Seyna, an AI chatbot in its mobile app](<https://srtb.bj/2025_02_17_anip_nouveaux_solutions_numeriques_faciliter_procedures_populations_prestations_ameliorees/>). [GPT BJ, the government's virtual assistant launched in 2023](<https://lamarinabj.com/index.php/2024/06/25/benin-une-expansion-en-vue-pour-lassistant-virtuel-gpt-bj/>), answers questions on the tax, digital, labour and penal codes. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the digital agency ASIN [put out a new version of the service-public.bj portal](<https://lanouvelletribune.info/2026/11/benin-le-portail-des-services-publics-fait-peau-neuve-avec-de-nouvelles-fonctionnalites/>). It carries Yemi, an AI assistant. ASIN's [legal note on generative AI](<https://asin.bj/doc/137/download>) is advisory. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of its AI systems.

[On 21 October 2025 the Ministry of Digital Transition and the broadcaster RTB signed an agreement](<https://news.broadcastmediaafrica.com/2025/10/23/burkina-faso-pioneers-ai-integration-in-public-broadcasting-with-rtb-partnership/>) to use AI to make public information accessible. In March 2025 the digital transition minister [told parliament her department was finalising three projects](<https://an.bf/127>). They are the Djam platform and two chatbots. One covers electronic communications regulation and the other legislative texts. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says any of them is in service. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service.

No stage is set as at November 2026. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether a government body in Botswana uses an AI system, has tendered for one, or is piloting or testing one. No source has been found that says no such system is in use. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source showing that a government body has tendered, piloted or is testing an AI system for its own work or its services.

[In March 2026 the government launched EMY 101, an AI assistant on WhatsApp, Messenger and toll-free number 101](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/cote-d-ivoire-launches-emy-101-ai-chatbot-for-public-services>). It gives information on civil status, taxation and ministerial services. In the last twelve months, on 12 October 2026, [the AI assistant Aya was demonstrated to the National Assembly's president](<https://www.koaci.com/article/2026/10/12/cote-divoire/politique/cote-divoire-assemblee-nationale-patrick-achi-ouvre-la-voie-a-lintelligence-artificielle-dans-le-travail-parlementaire_201534.html>), who tried it on budget analysis. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in a second government body. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

At a Minpostel workshop on 17 February 2026, the director general of the CNPS, the national social insurance fund, [said it uses AI](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/cameroun-avancees-piliers-et-dangers-de-l-ia-presentes-a-un-atelier-du-minpostel-dedie-aux-administrations-publics/>) for biometric identification, automatic customer response and an e-wallet. In July 2025 CENADI [unveiled GOV-AI](<https://www.dgb.cm/gov-ai-lintelligence-artificielle-gouvernementale-en-vitrine-au-sago-2025/>), an AI built into the nGomna platform that public agents use to consult regulatory texts. That makes two bodies with AI in service. The workshop is within the last twelve months. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need the government's authority for cross-government digital governance to issue rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or to publish a register of the government's AI systems.

[On 28 August 2026 the Ministry of Land Affairs told the Council of Ministers it was deploying a chatbot, Assistant Mimpa](<https://beto.cd/cadastre-numerisation-archives-foncieres-rntfi/>). It is meant to explain the land law to the public. That is the one dated fact found in the last twelve months. No source found says the chatbot is in service. None says any government body uses AI in service. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service or AI processing documents.

[In November 2026 the minister said the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy was the first in government to work with AI agents in its daily administration](<https://pp.itu.int/2026/en/itu_policy_statements/congo-rep-of-the/>). For now the agents are bought from the market. In September 2024 the DGPME opened [an AI-based information platform on business-support schemes](<https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7243556420925759490>) to users for testing. The minister's statement is within the last twelve months. No second body with AI in service has been found. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[In February 2025 Al-watwan reported that AI in the Comoros was limited so far to personal uses](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/intelligence-artificielle-i-les-comores-ne-disposent-toujours-pas-d%E2%80%99une-politique-en-mati%C3%A8re-d%E2%80%99ia.html>). An official of the national digital agency Anaden said the country had no national AI policy yet. No government body has been found with an AI system in service or under test. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Preparing would need a government body to tender for, pilot or test an AI system for its own work or its services.

[On 3 November 2026 the labour inspectorate launched its portal and management system](<https://www.inforpress.cv/en/nova-plataforma-digital-da-igt-permite-apresentar-queixas-laborais-e-solicitar-servicos-on-line-ministra>). The minister said its services include artificial intelligence features. In the last twelve months, the International Labour Organization says [the portal has an AI-powered virtual assistant on labour law](<https://www.ilo.org/resource/article/ilo-supports-digital-transformation-cabo-verde%E2%80%99s-general-labour>). In October 2025 the justice institute [demonstrated an AI chat on its Portal da Justiça](<https://justica.gov.cv/w/lisbon-forum-2025-destaca-inova%C3%A7%C3%A3o-digital-de-cabo-verde-com-o-portal-da-justi%C3%A7a-e-uso-%C3%A9tico-da-intelig%C3%AAncia-artificial>). Nothing found shows it in service. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[In June 2025 ANSIE presented a virtual assistant for the public procurement platform](<https://djibouti.un.org/fr/300071-djibouti-s%E2%80%99engage-sur-la-voie-d%E2%80%99une-intelligence-artificielle-inclusive-et-tourn%C3%A9e-vers-le>). It did so at an AI meeting backed by UNDP. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says an AI system is in service in a government body, or that the government has issued rules or a register for its own use of AI. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service or AI processing documents.

[On 29 April 2025 the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research launched the Private Digital Adviser](<https://www.univ-khenchela.dz/en/launching-new-digital-platforms-ministry-of-higher-education-and-scientific-research/>), an LLM-based system that answers queries on all the ministry's regulatory documents. In October 2024 the secretary general of the National People's Assembly said it [uses AI tools to transcribe and translate its debates](<https://asgp.co/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Wed-16-Oct-PM-Algerie-FR.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 shows rules or a register for the government's own use of AI. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of the government's AI systems.

[In September 2026 Egypt's AI council adopted a report counting more than 40 AI applications in use](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/25/egypt-ai-council-national-ai-strategy-quantum-computing/>) across government and banking. In October 2026 the head of the Consumer Protection Agency said it [uses AI to analyse complaints, inspection data, prices and online stores](<https://cairo.gov.eg/en/news/2026/october/22/ee7ef990fe2f40609756579de54d9b28>). In the last twelve months, in November 2026, FinTech Gate reported [Egypt's guideline for government procurement of AI systems](<https://www.fintechgate.net/258322>), adopted by the National Council for AI. It binds a contractor only where a tender document includes it. No rules binding government bodies' own use of AI, and no register, have been found. Mature would need such rules or a register.

On 12 October 2025 the Ministry of Revenues and the Ethiopian Customs Commission [unveiled eight digital systems, among them an AI-based customs chatbot](<https://addisfortune.news/revenue-customs-launch-eight-new-tech-systems>). Another was an AI passenger risk-management system. In December 2025 the Addis Ababa City Administration announced [an AI-enriched civil registration and resident services system](<https://www.ebc.et/english/Home/NewsDetails?NewsId=3422>), due to begin in 50 woredas. That announcement is within the last twelve months. Only the Customs Commission is found with AI in service. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[On 15 July 2025 the government announced the launch of Missamou, a chatbot on Facebook Messenger](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/le-gabon-lance-missamou-une-ia-conversationnelle-pour-moderniser-l-administration>). It uses natural language processing to answer citizens' questions on official news, public services and administrative procedures. It answers 24 hours a day from official databases. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in a second government body. None says the government has issued rules or a register for its own use of AI. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[On 26 May 2026 UNESCO handed over an AI-powered multi-hazard chatbot to the National Disaster Management Organization](<https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/ghanas-disaster-agency-turns-ai-reach-people-water-does>), which now owns and runs it. [Ghana Statistical Service's data science unit has built a machine-learning model that codes occupations and industries for its labour force survey](<https://www.data4sdgs.org/blog/why-africas-data-future-depends-nso-leadership>). That puts AI in service in two bodies. In the last twelve months, on 7 August 2026, the Accra Metropolitan Assembly [took over a migrant desk platform with an AI chatbot and live voice translation](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/accrametropolis_ama-iom-outdoors-multilingual-digital-app-activity-7495156166348660736-ljX7>). No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of the government's AI systems.

No stage is set as at November 2026. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether a government body in Guinea uses an AI system, has tendered for one, or is piloting or testing one. No source has been found that says no such system is in use. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source showing that a government body has tendered, piloted or is testing an AI system for its own work or its services.

[In April 2026 Permanent Secretary Cordu L. Jabang said The Gambia had launched an AI-powered fact-checking and verification system](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/04/gna-gambian-officials-highlight-ai-digital-transformation-in-modern-journalism/>), housed in the Ministry of Information. In October 2026 UNDP [launched e-Monitor Plus with the Independent Electoral Commission](<https://www.askanwi.com/news/undp-launches-e-monitor-plus-platform-to-safeguard-electoral-information-integrity-in-the-gambia>), which combines AI with human checks to monitor election misinformation. Both are within the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in two or more government bodies, or that rules or a register exist. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[In June 2025 a column in Ahora EG said the Ministry of Health had just launched Chatbot Guinea Salud](<https://ahoraeg.com/sociedad/opinion/2025/06/13/como-podria-mejorar-la-inteligencia-artificial-ia-la-gestion-administrativa-en-guinea-ecuatorial/>). The chatbot is a virtual assistant for public queries. The source is a newspaper column. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in a second government body, or that the government has issued rules or a register for its own use of AI. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[In April 2026 the Kenya Revenue Authority launched Shuru, an AI chatbot for filing tax on WhatsApp](<https://www.kra.go.ke/news-center/press-release/2362-kra-surpasses-ksh-2-trillion-revenue-milestone,-records11-4-growth-in-nine-months>). [On 10 November 2026 the Technopolis Development Authority launched the SecureKE Sovereign Security Operations Centre](<https://www.kbc.co.ke/kenya-launches-sovereign-cybersecurity-centre-to-shield-govt-systems-from-threats/>), which uses AI-enabled analytics across government networks. That puts AI in service in two bodies. Both launches are within the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the government has issued rules for its use of AI, or published a register. Mature would need the government's authority for cross-government digital governance to issue rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or to publish a register of the government's AI systems.

[In July 2026 a Central Bank of Liberia employee was reported to have invented an AI system for macroeconomic forecasting](<https://fpa.news/undp-reaffirms-commitment-to-liberias-digital-transformation-at-tech-summit/>). The bank is using it. In August 2026 the director general of the Civil Service Agency said [its information channels include an AI-powered virtual information assistant](<https://elbcnews.com/2026/08/06/civil-service-agency-launches-monthly-electronic-newsletter/>). Both are within the last twelve months, and they put AI in service in two bodies. No source found since October 2023 says the government has issued rules or a register for its own use of AI. Mature would need the government's authority for cross-government digital governance to issue rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or to publish a register of the government's AI systems.

The Audit Bureau head said it [began developing an institutional AI model, Diwan Bot, at the start of 2026](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=358534&lang=en>), to support auditing and oversight. In April 2026 the Minister of Labour and Rehabilitation was told that the ministry's [integrated digital platform, supported by AI, was about 30% complete](<https://ar.libyaobserver.ly/article/36835>). Both are described as still being built, and no source found shows AI in service in a government body. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. No other change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service or AI processing documents.

In October 2025 the Commissioner General of Revenue Services Lesotho said the authority [had incorporated AI into its customer service operations](<https://newsdayonline.co.ls/lesotho-cautioned-over-reliance-on-foreign-aid/>). It had [tendered for a generative AI customer relationship management system in July 2024](<https://www.rsl.org.ls/node/584>). The commissioner named no other agency using AI. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports rules or a register for the government's own use of AI. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

The digital transition ministry runs Idarati AI, an assistant that guides users through administrative procedures, and [LesEco lists it among the first working parts of a sovereign AI platform](<https://leseco.ma/maroc/maroc-ia-2030-le-royaume-passe-de-lambition-a-laction.html>) in September 2026. [The tax directorate uses a chatbot to assist taxpayers](<https://fr.le360.ma/economie/lia-encore-embryonnaire-dans-les-services-publics-selon-lexpert-marouane-harmach_G3KDUQCTCNCY5B6TUYNLU2LPVE/>), Le360 reported in September 2025. That puts AI in service in two bodies. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the minister said the ministry [had begun using AI to analyse about 2,800 administrative procedures](<https://al3omk.com/1208688.html>). No source found since October 2023 says the government has issued rules or a register for its own use of AI. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of the government's AI systems.

[We Are Tech Africa reports officials said in June 2026 that Madagascar's courts already use AI technologies](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/public-management/madagascar-develops-digital-criminal-records-platform-to-modernize-justice-system>). They use them for certain research and document management functions. The customs directorate says its [AI chatbot answers common customs questions all day](<https://www.douanes.gov.mg/la-douane-malagasy-a-la-foire-internationale-de-madagascar-cap-sur-la-digitalisation-et-lintelligence-artificielle-avec-le-tariff-et-le-chatbot-douanier/>). It showed the chatbot in May 2025. The June 2026 report is within the last twelve months. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need the government's authority for cross-government digital governance to issue rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or to publish a register of the government's AI systems.

In November 2025 the Banco de Moçambique [launched BmChat, an AI chatbot on WhatsApp, Facebook and its website](<https://www.diarioeconomico.co.mz/2025/11/24/trends/bmchat-o-assistente-de-ia-do-banco-de-mocambique-para-atendimento-permanente/>). It answers questions on statistics, credit data, interest and exchange rates and inflation at any hour. The report names no other public body with an AI system, in service or planned. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports rules or a register for the government's own use of AI. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

In June 2026 the Ministry of Youth Empowerment, Employment, Sports and Civil Service [launched Mourchid, an AI assistant in Arabic and French](<https://erribat.info/?p=80889>). It answers on jobs, the civil service and youth programmes. In December 2025 the authorities announced that [an AI road-safety system was operating on the national network](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2612-134553-la-mauritanie-met-en-service-une-solution-d-ia-dediee-a-la-securite-routiere>). The national police run it. Both are within the last twelve months, and they put AI in service in two bodies. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need the government's authority for cross-government digital governance to issue rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or to publish a register of the government's AI systems.

[The Central Informatics Bureau listed a government chatbot and mobile app, MAIA, among its operational systems in November 2024](<https://cib.govmu.org/Documents/Reports/List%20of%20Operational%20Systems.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the ICT ministry was [upgrading the chatbot into DIVA](<https://lexpress.mu/node/552290>), and Cabinet approved DIVA as the official chatbot for all ministries and departments. It is to roll out in phases, starting with 15 of them. No source found shows AI in service in two or more government bodies. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[UniPod Malawi said in 2026 that government ministries had submitted 18 AI use cases](<https://unipod.ac.mw/blog/applications-now-open-for-the-ai-for-public-good-challenge>) to its AI for Public Good Challenge. A panel shortlisted five and published them as challenges, which graduate teams are to build and test with ministry staff. In the last twelve months, that is the one dated fact found. No government body has been found with AI in service. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service or AI processing documents.

[In November 2023 the Prime Minister said the launched Digital Pocket Guide 2.0 has an AI chatbot, Pocketbot](<https://nbcnews.na/node/103524>). Through it civil servants get instant answers on public service HR policies. [In January 2025 a NUST master's thesis evaluated Pocket Bot as a self-service tool, interviewing 20 civil servants who used it](<https://ir.nust.na/items/97b0e777-f3f9-4918-8cfb-26a6cff001d3>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in a second government body, or that the government has issued rules or a register for its own use of AI. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

In May 2026 Nigeria [launched GovGuide](<https://techcabal.com/2026/05/22/nigeria-taps-meta-ai-to-help-citizens-access-government-services/>), an AI chatbot that gives government service information by voice and text. On 24 February 2025 the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency [announced Ask INU](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/nigeria-launches-ai-chatbot-and-self-reporting-portal-for-domestic-violence-survivors>), a WhatsApp chatbot. The Federal Ministry of Education [runs AskFME](<https://edtechhub.org/case-study/the-ai-adviser-who-supported-a-ministry-to-build-their-own-tool/>), an AI service desk on WhatsApp. In the last twelve months, in November 2026, the Anambra State ICT Agency [launched NORA](<https://von.gov.ng/anambra-unveils-digital-handbook-ai-assistant-for-residents/>), an AI assistant for residents' questions on state services. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of the government's AI systems.

The National Bank of Rwanda [deployed its Intumwa AI agent in 2021](<https://www.proto.cx/resource/rwandas-government-and-proto-partner-to-deploy-integrated-ai-citizen-support-agents>) to handle complaints across more than 600 financial institutions. On 4 November 2025 the Ministry of Infrastructure and the Rwanda Housing Authority [released an AI agent on Kubaka.gov.rw](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ishimwe-romalice_yesterday-our-team-at-the-rwanda-ministry-activity-7391804455949676544-5skC>), the national building-permits platform. That puts AI in service in two bodies. In October 2025 the Ministry of Local Government began designing the Mbaza AI agent for citizen complaints. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Mature would need rules for government bodies' use or purchase of AI, or a register of the government's AI systems.

In September 2026 Sudan's Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research [launched an automated chatbot on its admission.gov.sd portal](<https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202609250240.html>). It gives instant answers in Arabic to applicants for the 2026-2027 intake. In the last twelve months, that launch is the one dated fact found. Only the higher education ministry is found with AI in service, and no other ministry or agency is named using an automated assistant. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[Anta, the chatbot on the government's Service Public portal](<https://www.polygon.sn/anta-lia-au-service-du-citoyen/>), was built by Sénégal Numérique SA. It uses AI intent detection and voice recognition to guide users through administrative procedures. In the last twelve months, the procurement regulator ARCOP's [report of May 2026 on its APPEL platform's pilot](<https://arcop.sn/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Rapport_achevement_APPEL.pdf>) lists an AI assistant among the support given to users. On 5 October 2026 a court in Pikine-Guédiawaye [began work on a local AI application for judicial archives](<https://www.rts.sn/actualite/detail/a-la-une/justice-le-tgi-de-pikine-guediawaye-experimente-une-ia-pour-les-archives-judiciaires>) as a pilot. No second body is found with AI past pilot. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

EdTech Hub reported in July 2026 that the education ministry's delivery team [uses an internal WhatsApp chatbot built on GPT-4 most days](<https://edtechhub.org/case-study/the-graduate-who-brought-ai-to-sierra-leones-ministry-of-education/>) to pull teacher and pupil numbers and exam results. The Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education [had developed EDITH, an AI system for officials' information management, by March 2026](<https://thecalabashnewspaper.com/mbsse-develops-revolutionary-ai-platform-to-transform-education-management/>). Both are within the last twelve months. Only the education ministry is found with AI in service. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Operating would need AI systems in service in two or more government bodies, or one government-wide AI platform serving several.

[In September 2026 HoA DRIVE reported that the Somali Bureau of Standards is building an integrated management information system](<https://hoadrive.info/stories/somalia-standards-services-move-online/>) that includes a Somali-English AI chatbot to guide users through certification. In the last twelve months, that is the one dated fact found, and the system was still being built. No government body has been found with AI in service. No rules or register for the government's own use of AI have been found. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service or AI processing documents.

[In November 2026 the Eswatini Standards Authority and its partner AICE Africa said ESWASA is developing EswasaOne](<https://www.africa-newsroom.com/press/eswatini-standards-authority-and-aice-africa-launch-ai-safety-and-standards-center-of-excellence?lang=en>). It is a platform linking standards information, certification and inspection workflows. A conversational interface is among its planned features. That is the one dated fact found in the last twelve months, and the platform is still being built. Nothing found shows AI in service in any government body. Nothing found shows rules or a register for the government's own use of AI. Establishing would need a government body to use an AI system in service, such as a chatbot for a public service or AI processing documents.

Seychelles' border control uses the [FaceLane facial-recognition corridor](<https://www.travizory.com/travizory-celebrates-landmark-facelane-deployments>) for citizens and resident diplomats entering the country.
